# Generated Code Template

Use this template for generated C# text when the repository has no stronger convention.

```csharp
string source = $$"""
    // <auto-generated/>
    #nullable enable

    namespace {{model.Namespace}};

    partial {{model.TypeKind}} {{model.TypeName}}{{model.TypeParameters}}
    {
        {{generatedMembers}}
    }
    """;
```

## Rules

- Start generated files with `// <auto-generated/>` so analyzers and reviewers recognize generated output.
- Include `#nullable enable` unless the project has a different explicit convention.
- Build text with raw string literals or an indented writer (`PolyType.Roslyn`'s `SourceWriter`, or a small `StringBuilder` wrapper that tracks indentation). Do not build `SyntaxNode` trees with `SyntaxFactory` and `NormalizeWhitespace()`; it is slow and `AddSource` only accepts text anyway.
- Use `global::`-qualified names for framework and package types when generated code may live in arbitrary user namespaces.
- Omit the `namespace` declaration for types in the global namespace instead of emitting an empty one.
- Normalize line endings and sort generated members by a stable key.
- Make hint names unique by including enough namespace, containing type, member, or input-path information.
- For nested partial types, generate the full containing type chain. Preserve type kind (`class`, `struct`, `record`, `record struct`, `interface`), generic parameters, constraints, and namespace style. Note that a generic containing type such as `Outer<T>.Nested` cannot be named from a non-generic context, so extension methods for such types must declare the outer type parameters themselves (for example `ToStringFast<T>(this Outer<T>.Nested.Colour value)`); extension methods cannot live in nested types.
- If generated files are persisted for review, keep each file focused on one target type or concern.
